findings.location: externalPoint/exterior update at lines 300-313 and source/imported update at lines 325-347
findings.evidence: At p=.42, actual last visible donor-strand cylinder ends at [-1.9, .1918260179517014, .1007686311912453], while incoming-strand-0 begins at [-1.78, .06, .27]. Endpoint gap is .24579942066222854, versus .072 combined tube radii. No donor backbone segment joins the two through the open ComEC lumen. Additional uptake frames .30/.35/.48/.55 have .19719/.20954/.22010/.12901 gaps. Both homology options share this uptake code.
findings.whyWrong: The same entering DNA strand is depicted as disconnected external and internal molecules at the defining membrane-translocation step. It does not continuously traverse the drawn open single-strand pore.
findings.fix: Generate the external retained donor strand, the ComEC-transiting strand and the cytoplasmic strand from a continuous uptake path with shared exact junction endpoints; trim its moving ends continuously and keep degradation restricted to the other strand. Preserve later docking/D-loop behavior.
findings.verification: Reconstruct actual cylinder endpoints in both homology branches over uptake and near every clipping boundary. Assert a continuous nonbranching retained DNA path through the channel with no gap, duplication or imported DNA outside the one membrane, and deterministic irregular seeks.

findings.evidence: For endpoint t=1, the offset remains .18 at every pair<1 and becomes exactly zero at pair=1. Actual incoming-strand-34 end is [2.0729221256540944,.01028776704799412,.4199551412111008] at p=.8699999, then [2.0729221256540944,.010287767047994117,.23995514121110081] at p=.87: instantaneous .18 displacement while the object remains visible. Its preceding endpoint does not jump.
findings.whyWrong: The final DNA end snaps onto the chromosome instead of the strand-exchange front reaching it continuously. This is an actual geometry jump across a 1e-7 progress step, not merely an intentional visibility/stage change.
findings.fix: Use a pairing-front offset whose final endpoint tends continuously to zero as exchange completes, while preserving local resident displacement only after input contact.
findings.verification: Sample actual endpoint positions immediately around .87 with shrinking epsilon; displacement must tend to zero, not .18. Also retain exact final heteroduplex boundaries, contact-before-displacement and no-homology behavior.
